title: One pass through the tree: a verdict for each branch, once
outcomes: Builds a tree in a fixed order, forcing candidates first, with one verdict word per branch
Does not reopen a finished branch unless a missed reply turns up
Compares his verdicts with the engine line afterwards, verdict against verdict
Recognises a quiet position where a tree finds little

steps.text: **Fill each branch once.** In *The analysis tree: fill each cell once* you built a table. Now the lines are five plies and the positions are unlabeled. Work in a fixed order: forcing candidates first, each reply in turn, one verdict word at the end of each branch. **Do not reopen a finished branch** unless you find a reply you missed. Afterwards compare your verdicts with the engine line, verdict against verdict. Seven matches in ten is the target.

steps.caption: White to move. A tree with three rows. Qxf7+ ends in mate in three. Rxf7 does not mate; the engine puts it near +0.6 for White (depth 16), so a table would mark it slower, not bad. Bxc4 gives up the attack and the engine rates it about -6.9 for White. Row one is the only row with the word mates, so the tree is finished after one pass.

steps.text: **Two ways it breaks.** One: you go back over a branch you already judged because the next one feels uncertain. That repeats work and starves the new branch. Write the verdict and move on. Two: you stop because the list of replies looks complete; a reply you never thought of makes the table look finished when it is not. In a quiet position few branches end in a verdict. Both are rules of thumb.

steps.title: Same row, one knight added
steps.prompt: In the first position the Qxf2+ row ends in mate. In the second a white knight stands on f4 and everything else is the same. Fill the Qxf2+ row first: is it still best? In the third, would a tree find anything?

steps.text: **What the app does for you now, and when it stops.** Each exercise has three hints. The next three are silent: no hints and no engine line before you answer. Fill your table on paper first. Not every position has a tree worth building; say so when it does not. Hints on request only is planned, not built.

steps.text: **Revisit count: ten minutes, away from the app.** Take five positions with a forcing line from a puzzle book. For each draw a table and put a tick beside each branch when you judge it. Each time you go back to a ticked branch, make a mark. After five positions count the marks: your aim is zero. Then check with the engine or the book. A mark is not an error, only a sign of thinking inertia.
